SETUP YOUR SOCIAL MEDIA MAGNET PLUGIN

Go back out to your WordPress Dashboard and click on the “Plugins” menu item, and click on “Add New”

Next, click on “Upload Plugin”

 

Next, you must download the Social Media Magnet plugin from our website.  The link to download the plugin is immediately below this text:

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE SOCIAL MEDIA MAGNET PLUGIN another window will open to download the Plugin .zip file

Note, the plugin is named “Westgate-Analytics.zip.”  Yes, it is a .ZIP file.  DO NOT UNZIP IT!  Just save the .ZIP file to your desktop.  We will now upload the whole .ZIP file to your website. If your browser wants to unzip it automatically, which is common with the Safari web-browser, then please switch to Google Chrome or Firefox to download the zip file in its entirety.  You must have the file saved in its .zip file format.

Next, after you have clicked on the “Upload Plugin” button in WordPress, you will drag the .ZIP file on your desktop over into the file upload area and hover it directly over the “Choose File” button OR you can click the “Choose File” button and just select the file off of your desktop.  Either way is fine.

Once the file has been uploaded into the Choose File selection screen, click the “Install Now” button

When the plugin has been uploaded to your website, then click the blue “Activate Plugin” button.

Your plugin has been installed and activated. Before going to the next step, confirm that you have the latest version of the Website Analytics Plugin and update it if necessary.

Now go back to your WordPress Dashboard and click on the “Website Analytics” tab and then just underneath it, click on “Settings.”  The first grey tab that you will see open is the tab entitled "Social Media Magnet Authorization."  This is where you are going to add your Access Token from your Member Profile page at https://socialmediamagnetpro.com/member-profile/.  Click on the link to the left to go to your Member Profile page (located under Membership Details in your home screen).  Scroll down to the Class Info Section, as seen below.

First, make sure that your Practicum GMail EMail AND your Practicum Website URL are correctly listed in your class info.  Make sure that when you complete the Practicum Website URL field, that you cut out the URL directly from another browser window that you have open to your home page.  The home page URL to your site and this Practicum Website URL absolutely MUST be identical.  Cut and pasting is the best way to confirm that they are the same.  Now that you have these fields confirmed, you will move onto the Access Token.

At the bottom of the Class Info section, you will see a blue "Regenerate" button next to your Access Token option.  Since you are now setting up your Access Token, click the "Regenerate" button.  This process will create a new token for you that looks like this:

Click the "copy & paste" button to the far right of the access token letters.  This will copy the entire token for you so that you can paste it in its proper location in just a minute.

VERY IMPORTANT STEPS:  First, click the blue "UPDATE" button to confirm your access token.  When you click the update button, the token code will say "Updating..." and then it will disappear prompting a message that says "Updated Successfully."  Once it has updated successfully, then scroll down the page just a bit to a blue button that says "Update Member Profile."  Click this button to save the new token settings into your profile. From this point forward, you NEVER want to "Regenerate" your token again, otherwise, your Magnet Analytics on your dashboard will NOT report correctly.  You should only do this once during this setup.

Now that your access token has been copied into your cache, return back to the previous browser window (keep this window open) to the Plugin Settings for the Website Analytics Plugin.  Demonstrated below, you will PASTE the previously copied Access Token code into the field labeled "Access Token."  Once it is pasted, click the blue "Save Changes" button.  This should turn the Red X that was next to the "Access Token" label to a GREEN Checkmark as seen below.

Next, at the top of your WordPress dashboard, in a black menu bar that runs horizontally across the page, there is a menu item called "Managed WordPress."  Now that you have the green checkmark, click on the "Managed WordPress" menu item (located just under the address bar in your web browser).  It will create a drop down menu for the selection called "Flush Cache."  Click on it to flush your website's cache.  After this has been completed, you will see a block box appear with the words, "Success - Cache Cleared."  Close this box.

Finally, go back to the web-browser window open with your student profile. Hit the refresh button on your web-browser to refresh the page.  Once the page has been refreshed, you should also see a green checkmark down next to the "Access Token" option.  Once again, once this green checkmark appears, NEVER regenerate your access token again.  We want it to stay the same indefinitely from here on out.  Congratulations, you have completed the Access Token Handshake.  Your website is now authenticated!  Now, let's go back to the other window and finish completing all of your "Website Analytics: Settings."

As seen below, the next grey tab in your "Website Analytics: Settings" is called "Practicum Settings."  There is nothing that you need to do here.  But do realize that the dates for your Practicum Start and End will be displayed here.  These are set by your professor within his/her dashboard.  If you don't see dates here, then you need to remind your professor that he/she needs to enter the Practicum Start and End dates into their professor dashboard.  When the dates are entered by your professor, they will appear this way:

The third tab, called the Google Analytics Authentication tab, will connect your Magnet Analytics to Google Analytics.  Click on the “Click Here to Authenticate” link on the screen.

A secondary window will open asking you to choose the google account you want to authenticate.  Be sure to choose your BRANDED GMAIL ACCOUNT that we used earlier to set up Google Analytics.  When you select that account, the window will require you to allow permission.  Click the blue “Allow” button.

Upon clicking the Allow button, Google will provide you an access code.

It will be a long, scrambled code.  Copy this code and paste it into “Your Access Code” back in the Google Analytics Authorization tab in your Website Analytics tab in your WordPress Dashboard, like below.

Click “Save Changes” to save your Access Code.

Next, under the Google Analytics Profile tab, select your website URL from the dropdown list.  Click Save Changes.

Next, open a different browser window or new tab.  Log in to your SMM account (like you would be accessing your online textbook).  In your SMM Dashboard, click on "Membership Details" to open your SMM profile.  In this profile, be sure to check and make sure that your Google Analytics Profile selected from the dropdown (just completed in the picture above) is the exact same as the Practicum URL that you listed in your Social Media Magnet Profile.  These two need to be identical for your plugin to gather the Google Analytics Data correctly.  If they are the same, then you are good to move onto the next step.

Setting Up Your Mailchimp Settings in the Website Analytics Plugin Settings

Next, go back to the plugin window that you currently have open.  Click on the Settings tab.  Under this tab, we will have a few things to look up and input from your MailChimp account.  Now, go open a new browser window, and log into your MailChimp account that you established previously.

First, click on your name in the upper right-hand corner, and choose Account from the drop-down menu.

In the account menu, click on the “Extras” drop-down menu and select the “API Keys” option.

In the API keys menu, copy your API Key, just like you did in previous steps.

 

Paste this key into your MailChimp Settings tab of the Website Analytics Plugin Settings:

Next, go back to MailChimp, click on your name in the upper right-hand corner, but click on “Profile” this time.  In the Profile screen, copy your username.

Paste your username into your MailChimp Settings tab of the Website Analytics Plugin Settings:

Next, go back to MailChimp, and click on Audience in the Top Menu of your MailChimp FrontPage.  Make sure your actual list (e.g. Professor Members), is listed in the current audience.  Next, click on the Manage Audience dropdown button to the right.  In this dropdown menu, click on Settings.

Next, in the settings screen, click on “Audience name and defaults”

On this screen, copy the Audience ID in the right-hand column.  It is in RED letters.  Do NOT copy the "." at the end, or your plugin will not function correctly.

Next, paste this Red List ID into your MailChimp Settings "List ID" of the Website Analytics Plugin Settings:

Updating MailChimp Campaigns List

Finally, this next step will be automatically completed AFTER EACH WEEK that you compose and send out an email to your MailChimp audience.  You cannot proceed with this step at the moment because you haven’t started your email campaign, but we are going to show you how this works now, while we are discussing The Social Media Magnet plugin.

After EACH email that you send out from MailChimp, our Website Analytics Plugin will automatically update your MailChimp Campaigns List each Sunday night when the software runs and collects each student's data.  If you are impatient and want to see the campaign ID immediately populated into the Campaigns list after you send out the email, then you can simply hit the "Update Mailchimp Campaigns List" button, as seen below, at the bottom of the "MailChimp Settings" screen.

When you hit this button, it will update the Email Campaign IDs from your most recent emails since your last update (i.e. the last Sunday night software run or the last time you hit the update button previously).  These campaign IDs will now be automatically listed in the list of email campaign IDs (as seen below).  Please note that you can only launch 12 emails during the total length of your campaign.  For an 8-week campaign, that equates to less than two emails per week.  The expectation is that you will have at least one email a week, but have the opportunity to launch a second email every other week if desired.

CONGRATULATIONS!  You have now completed the Student Website Setup Instructions.  Your website is mechanically set up and ready to collect data.  But what about how it looks?  And how do I get people to visit my site?  See the beginning notes below, but the rest of our course will be based on these questions.

Final notes regarding the aesthetics of your website and the inbound traffic for your site:

Regarding Aesthetics:  Remember, this instruction set only helps you set up your website to mechanically run the Social Media Magnet way.  None of these instructions deal with the aesthetics of the website.  To make your website LOOK the way that you want it to look, then you will need to spend as much time or more working on the look of the site.  This starts with the Thematic Appearance of the site, which can be accessed in your WordPress Dashboard under "Appearance" --> "Themes."  If you don't like any of the pre-installed themes for your WordPress install, then you can click the "Add New" button at the top of this page and it will open up a whole host of options for you that are WordPress approved.  If you don't like those, then you can Google "Mobile Responsive WordPress Themes."  Be sure your options are all MOBILE RESPONSIVE.  This is very important!  You must choose a Mobile Responsive Theme!  What are themes, you may ask? Themes are like skins or clothes.  You can try on as many skins or themes as you want, but you must eventually settle on a theme that best represents the look and feel that you want.  Note: Not all themes are created equal.  Some themes have specific functionality that other themes don't have.  You are welcome to ask your professor about his/her preferred themes or ones that have worked well in the past, but note, no professor can tell you all of the functionality of every theme.  It's just not possible.  So you will need to experiment with most likely many different themes until you find the one for you.  It's a trial and error process.  Don't get frustrated, the more skins/themes you try on, the more you will learn what features and functions are a necessity, and which ones are not.  You will find your perfect theme, be patient in your search.

Regarding Inbound Traffic: You will also need to start setting up your own branded social media channels.  While you may use your own social media channels to move people in your social networks to your website, you MUST create your own branded channels for each social channel you expect to use.  Use your new branded Gmail (email) account that you created in the topical brainstorm assignment to set these branded channels up.  For Facebook, you will have to create a branded company page on your personal social account though, as you have to have a personal page to set up a branded page.  However, this page is anonymous and no one will be able to tell that it is connected to your account.  The point to each of these branded accounts is about message harmony.  If you only use your personal accounts, then your personal messages get mixed in with your branded messages causing your brand to become an OFF message.  We will talk more about On and Off messages later, but you must keep these harmonious and serialized messages separate from your own personal views.  Therefore, for an organic campaign to stay ON BRAND, it MUST have it's own branded pages for messaging.  For every social channel you use, your brand should have its own page for content creation and curation.  Yes, you will see a bump in your practicum scores over the first two weeks due to your own personal networks, but that bump will run out.  After that, it’s all about content creation and curation.  Without great content, your projects just will NOT organically grow.  Remember, this ALL about organic content.  Your blogs and social posts MUST stay consistent with your content calendar, holding to the promises that you have made to your readers about content scheduling.  No consistency equals no growth – Period!

Now let’s start making that website aesthetically beautiful and start building those social channels to entice as many users as possible to come to your website.  You have done all this work getting it set up correctly, now let’s make this website work for you!  How do we do that... With Engaging Content!!!

MAILCHIMP:  It is now time to set up your MailChimp Account for your email campaigns.  Note, MailChimp has recently changed the nomenclature within the platform for "List" to "Audience."  That is, since June of 2019, they use the labels "list" and "audience" interchangeably.  In some of the instructions below, if the instructions say "list" and you see "audience" within your actual MailChimp screen, then it is the same thing.  They have not changed the language over within the entire MailChimp platform yet, so you need to be aware that they mean the same thing in the land of MailChimp.  Sometimes they use "list" and sometimes they use "audience."  They are the same thing.  Just be aware.

SETUP YOUR MAIL CHIMP EMAIL SERVICE

  • Visit the MailChimp website: https://mailchimp.com/ Click on “Sign Up Free” button in upper right-hand corner Sign up using their form:
    • Insert Your New Project Gmail
    • Create a Username
    • Create a Password
  • Go to your Gmail account and approve MailChimp to activate your account.
  • After you activate your account, return to MailChimp online to set up your COMPLETE user profile.  Follow these instructions exactly:
    • Click on your account profile button in the top right-hand corner of the screen, and from the drop-down select "Account" as demonstrated below.

    • Next, click on the "Settings" drop-down menu and select "Contact Information" as seen below:

    • Next, complete your "Contact Information - Profile" by clicking on the "Edit Profile Information" button highlighted in red below.

    • Finally, complete your "Primary account contact" information.  You MUST put a physical address into this contact information.  In fact, this is a Federal Law!  If you do NOT fill out this information, then your API key in the steps below will not work.  If you do NOT want to put your own physical address that others will publicly see, then you may put your University's physical address in the address field.  But do be aware that whatever you put in this address will be publicly available on every email that you send out for this project.  Remember, it's a federal law!

WARNING:  Again, one last time, you MUST complete your profile setup process in the online account for MailChimp before you complete the Plugin Instructions below.  If you do not complete the entire setup process, including all stages of your profile information, then your API connection key may not connect causing an error message.  This may slow down your website build and even add to your practicum workload for the workaround solution.  Therefore, please complete your MailChimp profile before moving to the next step.  You have been warned!

ADD MAILCHIMP PLUGIN TO YOUR WORDPRESS SITE

  • Go to your WordPress Dashboard and click on “Plugins” in the black left-hand sidebar.
  • Click on “Add New” to add a new plugin
  • Search New Plugin “MailChimp for WordPress” > It’s this plugin:
  • Install Mailchimp for WordPress by clicking the “Install Now” button.
  • Once installed, click on the “Activate” button to activate the plugin.
  • Now “MailChimp for WP” will appear on your Dashboard in the black left-hand sidebar.

GET API KEY FOR MAILCHIMP

  • In the left-hand sidebar on Dashboard, Click on “MailChimp for WP"
  • Under this plugin on your dashboard, the primary page says “General Settings.”
  • In the middle of the page, click the hyperlink that says “Get your API key here.”
    • See annotated red box below for URL link:

Clicking on the link above will open a browser in the MailChimp admin screen.  Scroll down a bit and click on the gray “Create a Key” button as demonstrated below:

This will create your API key.  Cut and paste the API key from MailChimp, like so:

And Paste into your “MailChimp for WP” WordPress Dashboard Plugin into API Key Field, as seen below:

Be sure to click the blue “Save Changes” button.  This will create a Status that says “CONNECTED” within a Green Box.  This means it worked!  Woo Hoo!

If you do NOT connect, then you will likely get a message that looks like this:

If you get this error message, then you need to fill out the Contact Us form to alert us of the issue.  We will work with you to amend the problem or create a work-around for this 503 Service Unavailable error.

BUILD YOUR FOLLOW ME FORM IN MAILCHIMP

In the left-hand sidebar on Dashboard, Click on “MailChimp for WP”

  • Click on the “Form” tab.
  • Name the form “Follow Me”
  • Be sure that the list from your MailChimp account is CHECKED.
  • Click the blue “Add New Form” button

In the list of form fields that appear, click on “First Name”.

  • When the dialog box opens, make it a required field and click on the “Add to Form” button.
  • In the list of form fields, click on “Last Name”
  • When the dialog box opens, make it a required field, and click on the “Add to Form” button.
  • Lastly, in the “form code” to the left of the form preview, rename the “value” of the submit button to whatever you like, e.g. “Subscribe to my Email List”
  • Click the blue “Save Changes” button to record your changes.
    • When finished, it should look like this:

Next, click on the “Settings” tab just under the Title of this MailChimp Form.  As seen here:

  • Be sure to check the box next to: “Lists this form subscribes to”. This will make sure that when people hit the submit button on your follow-me form, their name and email will be added to your subscription list at MailChimp. THIS IS VERY IMPORTANT!!!  Otherwise, they will never be added to your list.
  • Next, be sure to click “NO” next to “Use Double Opt-In?”  I do recommend using this in the long term, but for the short term, during this course, this will greatly diminish the number of people who subscribe because the double-authentication email will get lost in the Spam, Junk, and Promotions folders of your wanna-be subscribers.
  • Click “YES” next to: “Update existing subscribers?” and then “NO” next to: “Replace Interest Groups?”
  • Next, scroll down. Under the Form Behavior section, there is a setting called “Redirect to URL after successful signups.” In this form field, you need to paste PERM B (the permalink from your Follow-Me-Thank-You Page previously saved into a Word Doc.  It should look like this:  http://www.[your-website.com]/follow-me-thank-you/, except where the [your-website.com] is, you will insert your website URL. Again, paste PERM B into this form field.
  • Finally, click the blue “Save Changes” button to record your changes.

CONNECT YOUR MAILCHIMP SIGNUP FORM TO YOUR FOLLOW ME PAGE

  • After you click the blue “Save Changes” button on the MailChimp Form, scroll to the top of the page.
  • Now copy the shortcode just below the Form name at the top of the page. It should look similar to this: [ mc4wp_form id=”15″ ].  See screenshot for the exact location of the shortcode:

  • Now, go back to your Follow Me Page, by clicking on “Pages” then click on your “Follow Me” Page.
  • Below your instructions of “Please fill out the following form below to receive my email updates”
    • Paste the MailChimp for WP shortcode.
    • Click the “Preview Changes” button to see what your Follow Me page will look like now that you have posted the MailChimp shortcode.  It is always a good idea to preview a page before you publish the update.  The preview should show your new MailChimp Email Subscription Form on-page.
  • Then click the blue “Update” button to publish the update to the page.  Note:  This is very important! Always “Update” any changes you make on-page or it won’t save. Thankfully, WordPress always has a pop-up window that asks if you are sure you want to leave when you haven’t saved your changes. Thank you, WordPress!

SETUP YOUR EMAIL SUBSCRIPTION GOAL IN GOOGLE ANALYTICS – VERY IMPORTANT!

  • Next, open a different web browser and go to “www.google.com/analytics”
  • Sign in with your Branded email account (Your created Gmail account from the beginning of the semester)
  • Click on the admin gear at the bottom, it looks like this when your cursor hovers over it:

This will open up your Admin screen that looks like this:

In the third column under view > Go to Goals > Click on Red “+ New Goal” button on your screen.

  • Goal Setup:
    • Choose the radio button of “Custom” > Click Blue “Continue” Button
  • Goal Description:
    • Name the goal, e.g. “Follow Me Thank You”
    • Type: Select “Destination” > Click Blue “Continue” Button
  • Goal Details:
    • In the Destination field: Add the thank you permalink (PERM B), but only the page, not the whole URL, e.g. “/Follow-me-thank-you/”
    • Funnel: Turn Slider to “On”
      • Step 1:  Add Name: “Follow Me”
      • Screen Page:  Add the follow me permalink (PERM A), again, not the whole URL e.g. “/follow-me/”
      • Step 1 Required Slider: Turn Slider to “YES”.
  • When completed, it should look like this:

  • Click the Blue “Save” Button.  Your two-step goal for “Follow Me Thank You” has now been set up.

CREATE YOUR CONTACT-ME AND CONTACT-ME-THANK-YOU PAGES

Just like with your Follow-Me and Follow-Me-Thank-You Pages, you are going to create a Contact process.

  • On your WordPress Dashboard, click on “Pages”
  • Search for a “Contact Us” Page that may have been created by the WordPress Install.  NOTE:  If a "Contact Us" page was not created during the install, then click on "Add New" to add a new page called "Contact Us."  Once created, click on "edit" for the Contact Us page.  Note: Be sure to edit this page in Classic Editor, not Block Editor.  NOTE: All form pages should be completed in Classic Editor, not Block Editor.
  • In the text box, either keep their instructions or add your own instructions, like:
    • “Please fill out the form below to contact me.”
  • Then Click the Blue “Update” Button; This will save the current permalink for this page.
  • Once you publish the update, then copy and save for Google Analytics.
  • (Save into a Word Doc labeled as PERM C.  We will use it again later.)  It should look similar to this: e.g. http://www.regalthebeagle.info/contact/
  • Go back to “Add New Page”
    • Add Another New Page: Title this page “Contact Thank You”
    • Just like before, add a Thank You Message, e.g. “Thank you for contacting us with your concern.”
    • Click the Blue “Publish” button to create the page.  The permalink should look like: e.g. http://www.regalthebeagle.info/contact-thank-you/
    • Once the permalink is created, copy and save for Google Analytics (Save into Word Doc as PERM D.)

WORDPRESS PLUGIN FOR NINJA FORMS – NEEDED TO CREATE AND TRACK ADDITIONAL WEBSITE GOALS

For every other type of Survey Form and Google tracking goal, we will use Ninja Forms instead of MailChimp.  MailChimp was just for your Email campaign.  We will use Ninja Forms for everything else.

Ninja Forms is NOT already installed on this version of WordPress.  Therefore, just like you did when you installed Google Analytics, you will need to go back to your Plugins tab in your WordPress Dashboard.  Once you are at the plugins screen in your dashboard:

  • Click on the "Add New" button at the top of the page.
  • Type in "Ninja Forms" at the top right of the search screen in the "Search Plugins" text box next to Keyword.
  • You will need to Install and Activate the Ninja Forms Plugin now.  Choose the one that looks like this:

Once you have installed and activated Ninja Forms, then go back to your WordPress Dashboard.

  • Click on Ninja Forms In your WordPress Dashboard
  • Under Title, Click on “Contact Form” Hyperlink
  • Click on “Preview Changes” to see what this form would look like on your website.
  • Under Form Fields, you can add or delete any of the standard questions you like to this form.
    • Clicking the Round Blue “+” sign in the bottom left-hand corner will show you what you can add.
    • Clicking the Blue “Gear” icon on each question allows you to replicate or delete the question.
  • Select the Emails & Actions Tab at top of the page
    • Under Action Gears for Success Message > Completely Delete the Success Message
  • Now click the Round Blue “plus sign” (+) in the bottom right of the screen.
    • Under “Installed” > Select “Redirect” to add a Redirect Gear
    • Click on the new Redirect Gear
      • Under Action Name: Change it to “Thank You Redirect”
      • URL: Add the “Contact Me Thank You” Permalink URL (This is PERM D from above).
      • Select Done in the top right corner
      • PUBLISH:  Click the “Publish” button.  (NOTE: When it’s published, it will be gray in color.)

Next, Click on the “Admin Email” or "Email Notification" Action Gear.  They are the same thing.  Either email process will notify YOU, the admin user, that a form has been submitted.

  • Change the Subject of the Email to: “Contact Us Form Submission”
  • Make sure “{fields_table}” is located in the body of the email.  This will provide you the data that the user submits on the form.
  • Most important, put your new branded GMAIL address in the “TO:” form box.
  • It all should look like this:

  • Select Done in the top right corner
  • PUBLISH:  Click the “Publish” button.

Next, if there is an email that says "Email Confirmation" then HOVER over the blue action gear icon.  When you hover over it, then two more icons will appear, which is a blue trash can and a duplication icon.  When the trash can icon appears, click on the trash can icon to delete the "Email Confirmation" option in this form.  When you hit the trash can icon, this "Email Notification" process will disappear.

Next, click the Round Blue “+” button in the bottom right-hand corner.

  • Click on Email, as we are going to add a new email to this contact form process.
  • Action Name for this Email: “Notification Email Back to User”
  • TO:  Click on the “input field” button within the TO: field (looks like a gray checklist or book)
    • Hover over the “Email {field:email_###}” field and click it.  This adds the user’s email to the TO: Email field
  • Put your new branded GMAIL email address in the “REPLY TO:” form box.
  • Change the “Subject” of the email to:  Thank You for Contacting Us.
  • In the Email Message box, write a note to the user thanking them for contacting you.
  • When you have completed these steps, it will look like this:

  • Select Done in the top right corner
  • PUBLISH:  Click the “Publish” button.  (NOTE: When it’s published, it will be gray in color.)

Leave the Contact Form: Click the white “X” in the black box in the top right corner to get back to the Ninja Forms FrontPage.

  • Next, Copy the short code for the contact form.  Most likely it looks like this: |ninja_form id = 1|.
  • Now go back to your Contact Page by clicking “Pages” and then clicking on “Contact Us”
  • Below your Contact Us instructions in the text box, paste the Ninja Forms shortcode in the text box.
  • Click the “Preview Changes” button to see what your Contact Us Form will look like now that you have posted the Ninja Forms shortcode.  Again, it is always a good idea to preview a page before you publish the update.  The preview should show your new Contact Us Form on-page.
  • Click the Blue “Update” button to Publish Your Update.

SETUP YOUR CONTACT US GOAL IN GOOGLE ANALYTICS

  • Next, open a different web browser and go to “www.google.com/analytics”
  • Sign in with your Branded email account (Your created Gmail account from the beginning of the semester)
  • Click on the admin gear at the bottom, it looks like this when your cursor hovers over it:

This will open up your Admin screen that looks like this:

In the third column under view > Go to Goals > Click on Red “+ New Goal” button on your screen.

  • Goal Setup:
    • Choose the radio button of “Custom” > Click Blue “Continue” Button
  • Goal Description:
    • Name the goal, e.g. “Contact Us Thank You”
    • Type: Select “Destination” > Click Blue “Continue” Button
  • Goal Details:
    • In the Destination field: Add the thank you permalink (PERM D), but only the page, not the whole URL, e.g. “/Contact-thank-you/”
    • Funnel: Turn Slider to “On”
      • Step 1:  Add Name: “Contact Us”
      • Screen Page:  Add the follow me permalink (PERM C), again, not the whole URL e.g. “/contact/”
      • Step 1 Required Slider: Turn Slider to “YES”.
  • Click the blue “Save” button.  Your two-step goal for “Contact Us Thank You” has now been set up.

NOW TEST YOUR MAILCHIMP:

Go to your WordPress Website like a normal user (Not through the admin page)

Go to your follow me page

  • Fill out the form and submit the form to test it.  Be sure to use another personal email, NOT your branded GMAIL account as the email subscriber and the contact us form respondent.  You want to make sure that the emails are going to the correct email inboxes.

Next, log in to your MailChimp Account online.  Click on “Lists” in the top menu bar.  Now, click on your email list.  Your name and personal email address should appear in the list and the source should say “API” to confirm that the name was added through your API key on your website.  See the correct setup below:

If you see your email address and the Source as API, then your Follow Me form is working correctly.

NOW TEST YOUR NINJA FORMS PROCESSES:

Go to your WordPress Website like a normal user (Not through the admin page)

Go to your Contact Us page

  • Fill out the Contact Us Form and submit the form to test it.  Be sure to use another personal email, NOT your branded GMAIL account as the email subscriber and the contact us form respondent.  You want to make sure that the emails are going to the correct email inboxes.

Make sure it works:

  • The person who filled out the form should get an email (to your personal email address)
  • You, the administrator, should get an email (to your Branded Gmail address)
  • And if you go to Ninja Forms FrontPage, you can view submissions of any of your forms by clicking on the blue gear, and then selecting “View Submissions.”  See the screenshot below:

To set up any more forms, you would follow the same process as the Contact Us form in the Ninja Form Setup Process.  Also, don’t forget for this process, you need to create both the Form Page and the Form Thank You Page.  Finally, you will need to set up the Google Analytics Goal Tracking for the destination pages.  If you haven’t quite figured out why we do this yet, we want Google to track the flow of user traffic from one destination (the contact us form) to a second final destination (the contact us form thank you).  Again, tracking the flow of traffic on our website helps us learn how to improve certain traffic directing, goal-oriented processes so that we can audit if we are having our intended effects or not.  This can be true for all kinds of goals that we can track and measure within Google Analytics.  The key to good management IS GOOD DATA!
title: 2.A-4b MailChimp & NinjaForms Setup

Website Setup Instructions

Directions: To set up the mechanical operations of your WordPress website correctly (i.e. to run your campaign the SMM Pro way), you must follow these directions EXACTLY step-by-step.  Do NOT skip any steps in the process, or the website will NOT run correctly.  If your website ever crashes during this process and you can NOT get back to your dashboard, you can call our 24/7 customer tech support at 480-624-2500.  Only use this number if your website crashes.  If you have questions about the interpretation of these instructions, first Contact Us through our support email, or ask your professor directly after using the Contact Us email support.

NOTE: Many of the free-ware plugins that we use in conjunction with this course are provided by third-party providers.  Without notice, this provider may change their setup or installation processes.  Therefore, please realize that the instructions below are the most recent template for each of these setup processes.  If the instructions are not exact verbatim, it is mostly like because the provider has slightly changed the installation process on their end.  If you encounter a difference in process, feel free to use the Contact Us form to inform us of the change and we will do our best to correct it as soon as possible.  The main goal of this instruction set is for you to become comfortable in the WordPress Plugin environment, and help you use your critical thinking skills on how to set up your website to run mechanically well enough to collect data from your website visitors. If the instructions slightly differ from what's on the instruction set, try to work through the issue first, using your super-duper Sherlock Holmes' skills of deduction.  If you absolutely can't figure it out, let us know and we will be glad to assist you.

This whole process will take you somewhere between 4-6 hours to complete, so let's begin...
